title: Flat-term K-flat target lifts in a closed Grothendieck category
statement: Let C be a closed braided monoidal Grothendieck abelian category with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian, def-sfb-monoidal-category, lem-sfb-flat-term-kflat-functor]. Let D,I be unbounded integer cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and t:D→I a chain map. If D is categorically K-flat [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] and every Dⁿ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], there are N, v:D→N and c:N→I such that N is categorically K-flat with flat terms, c is a quasi-isomorphism, and v followed by c is chain homotopic to t.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, cone construction and final flat-terms assertion; the same proof works in the indicated closed Grothendieck category.

proof.text: Choose the native functorial flat resolution M→Cone(t), whose terms are flat and which is K-flat since it is the integer colimit of its bounded-above flat resolution pieces. Compose its augmentation with Cone(t)→D[1], and set N=Cone(M→D[1])[-1]. Complete the resulting square of distinguished cone triangles in the homotopy category. The third-isomorphism argument after localization gives the quasi-isomorphism c; fullness of the homotopy quotient lifts the two arrows to v,c, with the triangle commutativity giving the requested homotopy. These are the fully proved native resolution and cone-square constructions imported in the Lean proof; no unproved public ringed-site factorization theorem is applied.
K-flatness is stable under shifts and cones. Each Nⁿ is isomorphic to Mⁿ⊕Dⁿ, so exactness of tensor makes it flat.

theorem exists_flat_term_kFlat_map_factorization {D I : CochainComplex C ℤ}
    (t : D ⟶ I) (hD : (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso C (.up ℤ)).kFlat D)
    (hflatD : ∀ n, ObjectProperty.flat (D.X n)) :
    ∃ (N : CochainComplex C ℤ) (v : D ⟶ N) (c : N ⟶ I),
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso C (.up ℤ)).kFlat N ∧
      (∀ n, ObjectProperty.flat (N.X n)) ∧ QuasiIso c ∧
      Nonempty (Homotopy (v ≫ c) t)
